body: Front Mission 5: Scars of the War is Square Enix's PlayStation 2 tactical role-playing game, released in Japan on 29 December 2005. Its campaign follows Walter Feng through a military career shaped by the recurring conflicts of the Front Mission world. Wanzers again carry the fighting, with pilots and interchangeable machinery forming the squad the player prepares before a mission. The title's interest in the marks left by war gives continuity to that structure. The next deployment is another stage in a life rather than an isolated tactical exercise.

Action Points limit what each unit can do, connecting movement and attack to the resources available during a turn. Links allow nearby allies to support an action, making placement useful beyond the range of one weapon. A squad that has been carefully assembled still needs a formation that lets its parts cooperate. Between missions, bases and camps provide time to organise pilots and equipment. The player moves repeatedly between these two kinds of planning: deciding what the unit should carry, then deciding where it should stand when the fighting begins.

Shintaro Tamai directed the game, with Toshiro Tsuchida producing and Hidenori Iwasaki composing the score. It gathers mechanics and setting details from across the series into a campaign that looks back over its wars through one soldier's experience. The original release remained Japan-only. An English fan translation appeared in 2009, allowing another audience to follow the story. Within Front Mission, Scars of the War gives the tactical systems a particularly long view, connecting successive battles to the people who survive them and return to serve again.
